newsitem.title: USA: SEC's Levitt likes FASB's newly elected chairman.
newsitem.headline: SEC's Levitt likes FASB's newly elected chairman.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt said Tuesday the Financial Accounting Board's newly elected chairman, Edmund Jenkins, is an "excellent choice."

"He'll be able to stand the heat from the business and political communities alike as he manages the important challenges facing FASB, including establishing derivative accounting rules and addressing international accounting standards," Levitt said in a statement.

Levitt's comments came as the accounting group said it had named Jenkins, who recently retired as managing partner of the Professional Standards Group of Arthur Andersen LLP, to a five-year term beginning July 1.
One major task before Jenkins is to finish controversial accounting rules for firms to abide by when they use derivatives to offset risks.
Various drafts of these rules have been opposed by derivatives industry players, who have been influential with top lawmakers in their fight to curb approval of the rules.
Jenkins replaces Dennis Beresford who has chaired FASB since 1987.
